idiom_name: frozen dataclass state + reduce(state, action) + Store with callbacks (or Textual reactives)
implementation_notes: Python ships no store, so the realization is a small hand-written module: @dataclass(frozen=True) states and actions with dataclasses.replace for updates, a pure reduce(state, action) dispatching on the action type (match, isinstance or functools.singledispatch), and a Store holding the current state with dispatch and a subscriber list. UI frameworks each provide a lighter local substitute that replaces the classic structure - Textual's reactive attributes with watchers and messages, Streamlit's st.session_state with a full rerun per interaction - and server-side apps keep per-request state in the request cycle, so hand-writing the store is justified mainly for desktop/data apps that must share one state across screens and replay it in tests. A niche PyPI Redux port exists, but no dominant framework provides the structure, hence manual.
pitfalls: frozen=True is shallow: a list field inside the frozen dataclass is still mutable, so appending to it changes the 'old' snapshot - use tuples or copy on write.
Mutable default arguments and shared class-level defaults leak between instances; declare them with field(default_factory=...).
Reference cycles through subscriber callbacks (widget -> store -> widget) keep objects alive; hold weak references (weakref.WeakMethod/WeakSet) or unsubscribe explicitly.
The GIL does not make dispatch atomic across threads that interleave; guard the store with a threading.Lock when worker threads and the UI both dispatch.
